claims.statement: Irregular income is a legitimate mortgage segment rather than an automatic exclusion, but the bank must conduct a complete, verified, individualized assessment.
Document preparation and administrative support are within the legally recognized intermediary workflow, while statutory creditworthiness assessment remains with the creditor.
Business-income files require bank- and tax-form-specific evidence and activity history, creating a concrete checklist and policy-provenance problem.
There is a sufficiently large regulated intermediary channel to test enterprise distribution, but official headcount and revenue do not prove software spend or reachable independent seats.

FinPack and Lendi already control substantial workflow and distribution, so differentiation must be a measured JDG exception layer that integrates with or outperforms incumbent handling, not a generic calculator or document portal.

The safer initial boundary is deterministic document and lender-policy support with meaningful human review; applicant creditworthiness scoring would trigger materially stronger AI Act and GDPR scrutiny.
The proposed seat price, 1,200-seat scale, broker time savings, outcome-data access, and network conversion are unvalidated assumptions.

contrary_evidence: FinPack claims use by 70% of Polish mortgage experts and already covers 20-bank affordability calculations, common forms, direct bank integration, and credit-history checks.
Lendi claims 3,000 experts plus multi-bank application and document-list workflows, combining software with an installed distribution network.
The AI Act explicitly treats natural-person creditworthiness AI as high-risk, and EU case law prevents outsourcing consequential automated scoring behind nominal human involvement.
Each bank owns its formal assessment procedure, so broker-collected historical approvals may be incomplete, selected, noncausal, and quickly stale.
